impact:
T-008's gate rejected BOTH lockfile candidates and adopted candidate C (a write-once port allocation published via `link()`, plus a continuously held loopback listener adopted by the publication winner). The decision is recorded in `docs/v0.2-prototype-findings.md` and in T-008's own amended criteria — but the four downstream tickets that consume it were never updated, and each still instructs an implementer to build the rejected design. Verified by keyword count in the ticket JSON:

- **T-010** — inode x2, revalidation x2, pid, process-start-time, owner token. Its dependency and constraints require "pid + process-start-time + random owner token" ownership and "inode revalidation before every publish and unlock".
- **T-011** — lockfile x4, inode x4, pid x6, owner token x2, revalidation x4. The stale design appears in its state machine, failure tests, dependencies AND acceptance criteria, so implementing it as written rebuilds candidate B end to end.
- **T-012** — inode x4, revalidation. Requires inode revalidation on every fast-tier tick and describes losers of a lockfile race, neither of which exists in candidate C.
- **T-013** — takeover x3, expiry x3. Specifies expiring ownership records and stale-state takeover for reader leases; candidate C has no owner record and no reclamation step — that reclaim judgement is precisely the operation Node's syscalls cannot perform safely, and precisely why the lockfile candidates were rejected.

Why this is high severity rather than bookkeeping: T-008's whole purpose was to gate the design BEFORE these tickets commit, and its own hard constraint is "record the decision durably so T-010/T-011 consume it without re-derivation". A recorded decision that the consuming tickets actively contradict is worse than no record — the tickets are the operative instructions, and an implementer following T-011 as written would reintroduce the exact unsafe reclaim-a-dead-owner's-lock primitive the gate eliminated, while believing they were following the plan. T-010 is explicitly blocked on T-008, so this lands the moment T-008 closes.

Each ticket needs its lock language replaced with the adopted protocol: write-once allocation + continuously held listener; authenticated foreign-holder refusal that never re-allocates; `assertHeld()` immediately before every atomic commit with no intervening await; `onLost` terminating or permanently disabling publishing; and for T-013 a separate allocation and purpose namespace for the reader lease, acquired by holding its own listener, with contenders rebinding the persisted port after holder death. The residual-window obligations are already written up in findings section 3.5 and are binding on T-010/T-011.

Not fixed inline: rewriting four other tickets' scope and acceptance criteria is well outside T-008, and the autonomous guide directs out-of-scope problems to issues.
resolution: Duplicate of ISS-030. ISS-030 survives as canonical: it is older, is the ID the findings doc cites for the T-010 fsync conflict, and is a superset of this issue. ISS-033's verified specifics are folded into ISS-030 and the v0.2 re-spec drafts: the per-ticket inventory (corrected — T-012's shadow inode/size/mtime validation is legitimate and must be retained; only its lock-race dependency clause changes) and the replacement protocol (write-once allocation + continuously held listener; authenticated foreign-holder refusal that never re-allocates; assertHeld() immediately before every atomic commit with no intervening await; onLost terminating or permanently disabling publishing; T-013 reader lease on its own allocation + purpose namespace with rebind-after-death and bounded-wait-then-honest-stale). T-008's Risks reference to ISS-033 now points here and onward to ISS-030.
title: T-010/T-011/T-012/T-013 still specify the lockfile design that T-008 rejected
